title: Bank of America Launches "Double Dip" Offer, Supercharging First-Year Cash Back on Two Popular Cards
imageAlt: Bank of America Customized Cash and Unlimited Cash Rewards cards with travel imagery
author: Financial Adviser, Travelcardinsider
snippet: New cardholders can now earn up to 6% cash back on travel and other key categories, a significant, limited-time boost for U.S. travelers planning their spending.
content:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. – June 7, 2025 – In a strategic move set to capture the attention of savvy U.S. consumers, Bank of America has announced a substantial enhancement to two of its flagship no-annual-fee credit cards. Effective May 28, 2025, the Bank of America® Customized Cash Rewards and the Bank of America® Unlimited Cash Rewards credit cards will feature significantly boosted cash back rates for the first year of card membership. This creates a powerful "double dip" opportunity for new applicants, combining a generous sign-up bonus with elevated rewards on every dollar spent, with travel being a key focus.

This timely update positions these cards as formidable competitors in a crowded market, especially for individuals and families gearing up for summer vacations or simply looking to maximize the financial return on their everyday and travel-related purchases. The new structure appears designed to offer immediate and tangible value, a clear signal that Bank of America is competing aggressively for new customers. For the full details of this new offer, you can refer to Bank of America's official announcement on their cash back credit cards page.

The First-Year Rewards Overhaul: What’s New?

Bank of America isn't just dangling a standard sign-up bonus; it's fundamentally overhauling the earning potential of these cards for the first 12 months. This two-pronged approach—a welcome bonus plus a temporary rate increase—provides a compelling reason for consumers to consider adding one of these cards to their wallet.

Let's break down the specifics of what this "supercharged" offer means for you.

Deep Dive: The Bank of America® Customized Cash Rewards – A Traveler's Secret Weapon?

For U.S. travelers, the revamped Customized Cash Rewards card is the standout of this announcement. Its strength lies in its flexibility, allowing cardholders to choose their own high-reward category, which prominently includes travel.

Key First-Year Offer Details:

  • Sign-up Bonus: New cardholders can earn a $200 online cash rewards bonus after spending at least $1,000 on purchases within the first 90 days of opening an account.
  • Supercharged First-Year Cash Back:
    • Earn a remarkable 6% cash back in a category of your choice from a list that includes gas and EV charging stations, online shopping, dining, travel, drugstores, or home improvement.
    • Earn 2% cash back at grocery stores and wholesale clubs.
  • Quarterly Cap: The 6% and 2% bonus rates are applicable to the first $2,500 in combined spending each quarter across these categories. Once you hit that cap, you'll continue to earn a standard 1% on those purchases.
  • Unmatched Flexibility: You have the power to change your 6% category once every calendar month, allowing you to pivot your rewards strategy based on your upcoming spending.
  • After Year One: The rewards rates revert to a still-competitive 3% cash back in your chosen category and 2% at grocery stores and wholesale clubs, subject to the same $2,500 quarterly cap.

A Real-World Travel Scenario:

Let's imagine the Chen family is planning a cross-country road trip and a flight to see relatives. They apply for the Customized Cash Rewards card.

  • Month 1 (Planning): They select "Travel" as their 6% category and book $1,500 in flights and hotels. This earns them $90 in cash back ($1,500 x 6%).
  • Month 2 (The Road Trip): They switch their 6% category to "Gas and EV Charging Stations." They spend $600 on fuel during their trip, earning them $36 in cash back ($600 x 6%).
  • Ongoing Spending: They also spend $400 at grocery stores during this time, earning $8 ($400 x 2%).

In just two months, their combined spending of $2,500 has earned them $134 in cash back. Having easily met the minimum spend, they also secure the $200 sign-up bonus, bringing their total rewards to $334. The ability to earn such a high percentage on a broad travel category for an entire year is a genuinely powerful incentive. You can find the full list of eligible categories on Bank of America's card benefits page.

Deep Dive: The Bank of America® Unlimited Cash Rewards – Simplicity and Strength

For those who value simplicity and want to avoid the mental work of tracking categories, the enhanced Unlimited Cash Rewards card presents an equally compelling, straightforward offer.

Key First-Year Offer Details:

  • Sign-up Bonus: This card also features the same $200 online cash rewards bonus after a $1,000 spend in the first 90 days.
  • Supercharged First-Year Cash Back: Earn a flat 2% cash back on all purchases for the first year. There are no categories to manage and no caps on the amount of cash back you can earn at this rate.
  • After Year One: The card reverts to a still-respectable unlimited 1.5% cash back on all purchases.

This card is for the "set it and forget it" consumer who wants a solid return on every single transaction, from airfare and hotels to morning coffee and souvenirs, without having to plan their spending around specific categories. A flat 2% cash back on everything with no annual fee is a very strong baseline. You can find more details on the Unlimited Cash Rewards card here.

The Preferred Rewards Multiplier: The Ultimate Power-Up

What truly elevates these offers from good to potentially market-leading is the Bank of America Preferred Rewards® program. If you have a qualifying account balance with Bank of America or Merrill, you can earn a bonus of 25% to 75% on your credit card rewards.

Let's see the impact with the highest 75% bonus (Platinum Honors tier):

  • Customized Cash Rewards (at 6%): The 75% bonus transforms your 6% cash back into an incredible 10.5% on your chosen category for the first year (6% base + 4.5% bonus). This is an exceptionally high return for travel spending.
  • Unlimited Cash Rewards (at 2%): Your flat 2% cash back becomes 3.5% on all purchases for the first year (2% base + 1.5% bonus).

For eligible clients, this multiplier effect is a game-changer. You can check your eligibility for the Preferred Rewards program on the Bank of America website.

Financial Advisor's Take: Which Card Should Be Your Travel Companion?

As a financial adviser, my guidance is to look past the headline numbers and match the card to your personal financial habits.

  • Choose the Bank of America® Customized Cash Rewards if: You are a strategic spender. If you have significant, concentrated spending in one of the eligible categories (like travel or gas) and can consistently get close to the $2,500 quarterly cap, this card will yield the highest return. It’s also the clear winner if you are a Preferred Rewards member.
  • Choose the Bank of America® Unlimited Cash Rewards if: You value simplicity above all. If your spending is spread thinly across many different categories, or if you simply don’t want to track your purchases, the 2% flat rate provides excellent, hassle-free value for the first year.

Both cards carry no annual fee, making them low-risk options to add to your financial toolkit. You can view Bank of America's no-annual-fee card options here.

Important Considerations: The Fine Print

Authentic financial advice always includes a look at the terms. Remember that these supercharged rates are an introductory offer for the first 12 months only. After that, the earning rates revert to their standard, lower levels. Furthermore, the $200 bonus is often advertised as an online-only offer, so be sure to apply through the correct digital channels to secure it. You can review sample credit card agreements for general terms here.

Conclusion: A Timely Upgrade for Your Travel Budget

Bank of America's decision to supercharge its cash back cards is a clear win for consumers. The chance to earn 6% on travel or a flat 2% on everything for a full year—on top of a $200 bonus and with no annual fee—is a compelling proposition. If you have travel plans on the horizon or are simply looking to get more back from your spending, these enhanced offers are worthy of serious consideration.

title: This Insane 5 Free Night Hotel Offer from IHG is The Deal You Need for Summer
imageAlt: IHG One Rewards Premier Credit Card with a summer vacation backdrop
author: Travel Card Insider Staff
snippet: IHG and Chase are offering a massive welcome bonus of 5 Free Hotel Nights on the IHG One Rewards Premier Credit Card, a deal that could provide over $1,500 in value for summer travel.
content:
Look, we see a ton of credit card offers here at Travel Card Insider. Most are pretty standard, but every now and then, one comes along that makes our entire team sit up and pay attention. This is one of those times.

Right now, IHG and Chase are offering a welcome bonus on the IHG One Rewards Premier Credit Card that’s honestly one of the best we've seen all year. We're talking 5 Free Hotel Nights. Seriously.

In a world where hotel bills can seriously eat into your travel fund, the chance to get five nights completely free isn't just a deal—it's your ticket to a vacation you might have thought was out of reach. So, let's break down what this offer is all about, how to get the most out of it, and whether it’s the right move for you.

So, What's the Deal? Here’s the Lowdown

We love a straightforward offer, and this one is refreshingly simple. No weird rules or confusing math. Here’s exactly what you get and what you need to do.

  • The Card: It's the IHG One Rewards Premier Credit Card, issued by Chase.
  • The Bonus: You score 5 Free Night certificates after hitting the sign-up goal.
  • The Goal: Just spend $5,000 on the card in your first three months to unlock the nights [Link to Official Chase Card Application Page].
  • The Power of Each Night: Each certificate is good for a one-night stay at an IHG hotel that costs up to 60,000 IHG One Rewards points.
  • The Clock is Ticking: You have a full year from when the certificates are issued to use them, which gives you plenty of time to plan.
  • The Cost: The card has a $99 annual fee.

Quick heads-up: these 5 welcome bonus certificates are capped at 60k points. You can't add your own points to book a more expensive hotel. That feature is reserved for the card's annual anniversary night, which is still a great perk we'll get to later.

Why 5 Free Nights is Such a Big Deal

Okay, so what’s the real-world value here? While it depends on your travel style, you’re easily looking at a value of $1,500 or more. Think about it—a decent hotel in a major city can easily run you $300 a night. With this offer, you could cover a five-night trip or take several long weekend getaways without touching your wallet for the hotel stay. For a $99 annual fee, the value you get back in the first year is just massive. It's a travel-hacking grand slam.

Your Game Plan: How to Use These Nights Like a Pro

Getting the bonus is easy. Using it for maximum impact is the fun part. You want to use these certificates where they'll save you the most cash. Here are some ideas to get your gears turning:

  • The All-Inclusive Dream (Mexico): This is my favorite play. You can book the Holiday Inn Resort Ixtapa All-Inclusive for around 50,000 points a night [Link to IHG Hotel Directory]. Why it's great: Using your certificates here means your room, food, and drinks are covered. A five-night beach vacation for virtually free? Yes, please.
  • The Big City Break (New York City): NYC hotels are notoriously expensive, making it a perfect place to use your certs. Pro Tip: Look for off-peak dates at hotels like the InterContinental New York Times Square. If you can snag a room for under 60k points when cash rates are $400+, you're winning.
  • European Adventures (London or Paris): A trip across the pond can get pricey, fast. Using these nights can take a huge bite out of your budget. Where to Look: Check out cool, boutique-style hotels like the Kimpton Fitzroy London or a well-located Holiday Inn in Paris. Finding availability under 60k points means hundreds of dollars back in your pocket for food and fun.
  • Caribbean Vibes (Aruba): Picture yourself on a white sand beach. The Move: The Holiday Inn Resort Aruba is a popular spot that’s often bookable with points. Using a certificate here for a room that would cost a few hundred bucks is a fantastic feeling.

My Top Tip: Before you click "book," do a quick search for the cash price on your dates. If a room is only $120, maybe pay cash and save that free night for a trip where it can save you $300+.

More Than a One-Hit Wonder: The Card’s Everyday Perks

A huge sign-up bonus is awesome, but a card needs to be useful long-term. The IHG Premier keeps delivering value year after year. Here’s how:

  • Automatic Platinum Elite Status: You're instantly upgraded to Platinum Elite status, which gets you nice perks like room upgrades, bonus points, and late checkout whenever you stay at an IHG property [Link to IHG One Rewards Status Benefits].
  • Annual Free Night: Every year you keep the card, you get another free night certificate for hotels up to 40,000 points. Plus, with this one, you can add your own points to book even fancier stays.
  • Fourth Night Free: This is a killer perk. When you book 3 nights with points, you get the 4th night completely free. It’s an amazing way to stretch your points further.
  • TSA PreCheck / Global Entry Credit: The card will reimburse you up to $100 every four years for the application fee for these time-saving programs [Link to Official Global Entry Website].
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Never pay extra fees when you use your card abroad. A must-have for any traveler.

The Final Question: Should You Get This Card?

This offer is incredible, but let's make sure it's a good fit for you. Ask yourself these questions:

  • Can I handle the spend? Be honest. Is spending $5,000 in three months something you can do with your normal, everyday expenses? Don't go into debt for points.
  • Do I stay at IHG hotels? IHG's family of brands is huge, from Holiday Inn to InterContinental and Kimpton [Link to IHG Brands Collection]. If you're not opposed to staying with them, you're golden.
  • Is the $99 fee worth it after year one? The welcome bonus makes the first year a no-brainer. After that, the annual free night alone can easily be worth more than the $99 fee. For most travelers, the answer is a clear yes.
  • Am I eligible? Chase has rules about how often you can get a bonus [Link to Chase Card Agreement/Terms]. Generally, you can't get this if you currently have an IHG card or got a bonus for one in the last 24 months.

The Bottom Line

The IHG Premier Card's 5 Free Night offer is the real deal. It’s a straightforward, high-value bonus on a card that provides excellent long-term perks. If you can meet the spend responsibly and have travel plans in your future, this is one of the smartest moves you can make for your wallet right now.

title: The Bonvoy Shake-Up: Marriott Quietly Rewrites Elite Upgrade Rules, Putting Suite Upgrades on Shaky Ground
imageAlt: A modern Marriott hotel lobby, symbolizing the shift in Bonvoy elite benefits.
author: Travel Card Insider Staff
snippet: A subtle but significant change to the Marriott Bonvoy loyalty program's terms and conditions has sent a wave of concern through the frequent traveler community. The target of this revision? One of the most cherished perks for elite members.
content:
A subtle but significant change to the Marriott Bonvoy loyalty program's terms and conditions has sent a wave of concern through the frequent traveler community. The target of this revision? One of the most cherished perks for elite members. For our readers who strategically leverage their Platinum, Titanium, or Ambassador Elite status, this development is more than just fine print—it's a fundamental shift that could alter the value proposition of Marriott loyalty.

The change, which appears to have been rolled out between late April and mid-May 2025, centers on a few carefully chosen words that have been removed from the official policy. Here at Travel Card Insider, we've analyzed the change to give you a clear-eyed view of what this means for your future travels and your wallet.

The Devil in the Deletion: Unpacking the New Policy

At the heart of the issue is the language describing the complimentary upgrade benefit. For years, elite members have relied on a key phrase to advocate for better rooms at check-in.

  • The Old Promise: Previously, the policy stated that Platinum Elite members and above were entitled to a "complimentary upgrade to the best available room, subject to availability upon arrival." This section explicitly listed suites as a part of this benefit. That phrase, "best available room," was the cornerstone of many successful suite upgrade requests. If a standard suite was available for sale, members had a strong case that it was, in fact, the "best available" and should be theirs. For reference, you can see discussions of this past policy on travel blogs like Frequent Miler.
  • The New Reality: The updated terms have strategically erased that crucial phrase. The policy now simply reads that members will receive a "complimentary upgrade," with suites still listed as a possibility among other less glamorous options like rooms with better views or on higher floors, as seen in the current Marriott Bonvoy T&Cs page.

By removing "to the best available room," Marriott has shifted the power dynamic. The explicit mandate for hotels to offer the top-tier available room is gone, replaced by a more ambiguous promise of a generic "upgrade."

A Financial Advisor's Take: What This Means for Your Travel Strategy

This isn't just a matter of semantics; it has tangible consequences for how you should value your elite status and plan your stays.

The most immediate impact is the increase in hotel discretion. While many well-run properties will continue to reward top-tier members with generous upgrades to foster loyalty, they are no longer contractually obligated by the program's terms to do so. A hotel can now fulfill its "upgrade" duty by moving you from a standard king to a standard king with a "partial city view," even if a suite sits empty. This makes the upgrade benefit less predictable and, for some, less valuable.

This move brings Marriott's official stance closer to that of Hilton Honors, where suite upgrades are widely understood to be a discretionary perk. It's a step away from the more robust suite upgrade benefit that has long been a hallmark of World of Hyatt's Globalist status.

For travelers who previously used the "best available room" language as leverage at the check-in counter, that tool has been weakened. The front desk now has more official backing to deny a suite upgrade request.

Compounding this is another clause updated in May 2025, noting that "Local policy may prevail over Loyalty Program standards" at some properties. This adds another layer of uncertainty, potentially creating significant inconsistencies in how benefits are applied. This clause can be found within the general Marriott T&Cs.

The Real-World Impact: How Your Next Check-In Might Differ

Imagine this common scenario:

  • Before the Change: As a Platinum Elite member, you arrive at a resort and see standard suites available. You're offered a room on a higher floor. You could politely point to the "best available room" clause, and your odds of success were reasonably high.
  • After the Change: In the same situation today, the hotel is on much firmer ground. They can state that the high-floor room is your complimentary upgrade and that they have met their obligation under the current upgrade policy wording.

Your New Game Plan: How to Navigate the New Upgrade Landscape

This policy shift doesn't mean suite upgrades are a thing of the past, but it does mean you need to adjust your strategy.

  1. Re-evaluate Your Nightly Upgrade Awards (NUAs): These awards (formerly Suite Night Awards) have just become more valuable. If securing a suite is a priority, NUAs are your most reliable tool. Their value proposition has arguably increased, as the complimentary alternative at check-in is now less certain. You can find more details on Marriott's official Nightly Upgrade Awards page.
  2. Temper Expectations, But Still Ask: Go into every check-in hoping for the best but prepared for a more modest upgrade. It never hurts to ask politely about the possibility of a suite, but be prepared for the answer to be no.
  3. Rethink Your Credit Card Value: For those holding premium cards like the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® Card, which grants automatic Platinum Elite status, this is a slight devaluation of a key benefit. You must now weigh the card's annual fee against a slightly weaker upgrade perk. For some, a card like the Marriott Bonvoy Boundless® Credit Card, with its lower fee and path to Gold status, might present a different kind of value.
  4. Leverage Relationships: Now more than ever, loyalty that goes beyond the program matters. If you frequent a particular property, building a good rapport with the management can lead to recognition that transcends the written rules.

Final Thoughts from the Insider

Marriott Bonvoy remains a powerhouse loyalty program, and elite status still provides immense value through benefits like guaranteed late check-out, bonus points, and lounge access, as outlined in the general elite benefits guide. However, this adjustment to the upgrade policy is a clear signal that the program is evolving to give properties more flexibility and control over their premium room inventory.

The dream of a near-guaranteed suite upgrade on every trip may be fading. For savvy travelers, the key is to adapt. By understanding the new rules, strategically using your NUAs, and managing your expectations, you can still navigate the Bonvoy program to your advantage and make every stay a rewarding one.

title: United Overhauls MileagePlus: Are Your Elite Perks Safe? A Financial Advisor's Breakdown
imageAlt: United Airlines aircraft with MileagePlus branding, symbolizing program changes.
author: Financial Advisor, Travelcardinsider
snippet: United Airlines is initiating a landmark overhaul of its celebrated MileagePlus program. Effective August 21, 2025, instant upgrades on high-fare tickets and the Excursionist Perk will be discontinued, while PlusPoints gain major new flexibility. Here's what it means for you.
content:
United Overhauls MileagePlus: Are Your Elite Perks Safe? A Financial Advisor's Breakdown

NEW YORK, NY – United Airlines is initiating a landmark overhaul of its celebrated MileagePlus program, a move that will redefine value for its millions of loyal flyers. For years, travelers have built strategies around a specific set of valuable perks. Now, some of those are on the way out. Effective August 21, 2025, two of the program's most powerful features—instant upgrades on high-fare economy tickets and the popular Excursionist Perk—will be discontinued for new bookings. In their place, United is injecting powerful new flexibility into its PlusPoints system, transforming them into a true loyalty currency for its top-tier members.

This "give and take" marks a significant shift in United's loyalty philosophy. As a financial advisor focused on travel rewards, I see this as a calculated move to rebalance the scales. The critical question for every U.S.-based United loyalist is: are you a winner or a loser in this new landscape? Let’s break down the changes and what they mean for your future travels.

The End of an Era: Saying Goodbye to Two Coveted Perks

For the savvy traveler, MileagePlus was a system to be mastered. Two benefits stood out as pillars of exceptional value. Their retirement will fundamentally alter the travel calculus for many.

1. The Vanishing Instant Upgrade: Certainty Becomes a Coin Toss

For business travelers and last-minute flyers, the instant upgrade on full-fare (Y, B, and M class) tickets was a golden guarantee. Purchasing a more expensive, flexible economy ticket meant an immediate, confirmed seat in the premium cabin. This perk removed the stress of the upgrade lottery, providing a tangible return on a higher travel spend.

What’s Changing: As of August 21, 2025, this guarantee evaporates. Premier members on these fares will no longer jump the line. Instead, they’ll be added to the standard Complimentary Premier Upgrade (CPU) waitlist with everyone else, subject to the usual hierarchy of status and fare class, as detailed on the United MileagePlus Premier Benefits Page.

Real-World Impact: Imagine a Chicago-based Premier Gold consultant needing a last-minute flight to San Francisco. Previously, her company’s $800 flexible Y-class fare secured an instant First Class seat. After the change, that same $800 ticket only buys her a spot on the waitlist, likely behind numerous Premier 1K and Platinum members. The core value of that expensive fare is significantly diminished.

2. The Final Journey for the Excursionist Perk

Often called one of the best "travel hacks," the Excursionist Perk was the key to sprawling international adventures. It allowed members booking a multi-city international award ticket to embed a free one-way flight within their destination region, saving thousands of miles.

What’s Changing: This beloved feature will be eliminated for all award tickets booked on or after the August 21, 2025 deadline, a change noted in United's MileagePlus Award Travel Updates.

Real-World Impact: Consider a trip from the U.S. to Europe. Using the perk, you could fly to Frankfurt, add a flight to Rome for zero extra miles, and fly home from Paris. That "free" intra-Europe flight was the linchpin. Now, travelers must pay for that flight with cash or more miles, increasing the cost of multi-stop journeys.

The New Power Player: PlusPoints Get a Major Promotion

While these losses will sting, United is reinvesting the value directly into its most loyal tiers: Premier Platinum and 1K members. Starting mid-2025, the PlusPoints they earn will evolve from a simple upgrade tool into a remarkably flexible loyalty currency. You can learn more by visiting the United PlusPoints Program Details page.

This move gives elites unprecedented control over their earned benefits. The new redemption options will allow members to:

  • Gift Premier Status: Bestow Silver or Gold status on friends, family, or colleagues.
  • Buy Status: Use points for Premier Qualifying Points (PQP) or Flights (PQF) to secure your own status.
  • Convert to TravelBank Cash: Turn unused points into a cash balance for future United flights.
  • Exchange for Bonus Miles: Convert PlusPoints directly into redeemable award miles.

These options apply to points earned in the 2025 qualification year, ensuring that earned benefits no longer go to waste.

A Financial Advisor's Take: Winners, Losers, and United's Strategy

From a financial perspective, this is a brilliant simplification for United. They are trading complex perks used by a savvy minority for a more democratized system with broader appeal.

Who Loses?

  • The Itinerary Architect: The traveler who mastered the Excursionist Perk to craft elaborate, high-value trips loses their greatest tool.
  • The Full-Fare Business Traveler: The road warrior who paid a premium for the certainty of an instant upgrade now pays for a mere chance.

Who Wins?

  • The "Almost Elite" Member: A flyer just shy of requalifying can now use PlusPoints for PQP, saving them from expensive, last-minute mileage runs.
  • The Generous Elite: A Premier 1K member can now grant valuable status to a spouse or child, extending perks like free checked bags and Economy Plus access to their family.
  • The Pragmatic Elite: Top-tier flyers who often let PlusPoints expire can now convert them to cash or miles, ensuring no earned reward is wasted.

Your Action Plan: Navigating the New United Landscape

With the deadline ahead, proactive planning is essential. Here are my recommendations:

  1. Lock In That Dream Trip. If a multi-destination award trip is in your plans, you have until August 20, 2025, to book it and use the Excursionist Perk one last time. This is your final call on the United Airlines Booking Page.
  2. Rethink Your High-Fare Strategy. If you or your company regularly buys full-fare tickets for the upgrade, it's time for a cost-benefit analysis. It may now be more economical to book a lower fare and use PlusPoints to waitlist.
  3. Become a PlusPoints Strategist. For Platinum and 1K members, think like an investor. Is gifting status more valuable than a potential upgrade? Will a PQP boost save your status? This new system gives you choices—learn to use them.

A New Chapter for MileagePlus

United’s 2025 overhaul is a redefinition of its loyalty contract. The airline is shifting from rewarding niche expertise to empowering its top flyers with flexibility. While the loss of legacy perks will be felt, the rise of a more versatile PlusPoints system introduces a more practical era for MileagePlus. For the informed traveler, adapting to this new reality is the key to maximizing your returns in the friendly skies. Always refer to the official United MileagePlus Terms and Conditions for complete details.

title: Urgent Alert for Delta SkyMiles Members: Hawaiian Airlines Partnership Ends This Month, New Rule for Elite Benefits
imageAlt: Delta and Hawaiian Airlines logos signifying the end of their partnership.
author: Airline News Reporter
snippet: The clock is ticking on using your SkyMiles for Hawaiian getaways, and Delta has changed how its most loyal members claim their top-tier rewards. The valuable partnership between Delta and Hawaiian Airlines is officially ending on June 30, 2025.
content:
Urgent Alert for Delta SkyMiles Members: Hawaiian Airlines Partnership Ends This Month, New Rule for Elite Benefits

The clock is ticking on using your SkyMiles for Hawaiian getaways, and Delta has changed how its most loyal members claim their top-tier rewards. In the dynamic world of airline loyalty, two critical updates from Delta Air Lines demand your immediate attention. Whether you’ve been saving SkyMiles for a Hawaiian vacation or you hold elite Medallion status, these changes will impact your travel strategy.

First, the valuable partnership between Delta and Hawaiian Airlines is officially ending. The final day to book an award trip on Hawaiian Airlines with your SkyMiles is June 30, 2025.

Second, in a major operational shift effective June 1, 2025, Delta now requires that its coveted Medallion Choice Benefits be selected exclusively through the Fly Delta mobile app.

These are not minor tweaks; they fundamentally alter how you redeem miles for Pacific travel and how elite flyers access their best perks. Here’s the insider's breakdown of what you need to know and the actions to take now.

Last Call: The End of the Delta-Hawaiian Partnership

For years, the ability to use Delta SkyMiles on Hawaiian Airlines has been a fantastic route to the islands, opening up more flight options and award seats. This valuable link is now being severed. As Hawaiian Airlines integrates with its new parent company, Alaska Airlines, it is cutting ties with competing carriers. The relationship with Delta is the latest casualty, with all benefits ceasing at the end of this month.

What This Means for Your SkyMiles:

  • Booking Deadline: You must book and have your Hawaiian Airlines award ticket issued using SkyMiles on or before June 30, 2025. Your travel can be for a later date, but the booking must be finalized by this deadline [Source: Delta Air Lines News Hub].
  • The No-Changes Rule: This is the most critical detail. Any Hawaiian Airlines award ticket booked with SkyMiles cannot be changed after June 30, 2025. If your plans change, your only option is to cancel the ticket and have your miles refunded. You will not be able to rebook, making travel certainty paramount.

Real-World Scenario: The Holiday Vacation

Imagine you have enough SkyMiles for a family holiday trip to Maui on Hawaiian Airlines.

  • Action Required: You must book those tickets before midnight on June 30, 2025. On July 1, that award option will disappear forever.
  • The Risk: Once booked, your dates are set in stone. If you need to shift your travel, you can't just call and change it. You would have to cancel, get your miles back, and then hunt for new award flights on Delta, which could cost far more miles or have no availability.

This change also closes a loophole for savvy travelers who transferred American Express points to HawaiianMiles to book flights on Alaska Airlines. That indirect transfer path will also end on June 30 [Source: Hawaiian Airlines Newsroom].

Your Phone is the New Key: Choice Benefits Go App-Only

For Delta’s top-tier flyers, reaching Platinum or Diamond Medallion status unlocks Choice Benefits—a menu of high-value perks. As of June 1, 2025, Delta has mandated these benefits can only be selected through the Fly Delta app [Source: Delta Choice Benefits Page].

Choice Benefits are some of the best perks in the SkyMiles program, including Upgrade Certificates, bonus SkyMiles, gifted Medallion status, and Delta Sky Club access. The ability to choose your preferred reward is a cornerstone of elite status value.

Why the "App-Only" Rule Matters

The convenience of using your desktop computer to select these crucial benefits is gone. This is a deliberate strategy to push all members, especially the most engaged ones, toward deeper interaction with its mobile platform.

Real-World Scenario: The Business Traveler

A road-warrior Diamond Medallion member can no longer use her laptop to select her annual benefits.

  • Action Required: Her routine must change. She now must download the Fly Delta app, log in, and navigate to the Choice Benefits section to make her selections for the year. This is the only channel available to claim these high-value rewards [Source: Fly Delta App Information Page].

The Insider's Take: Strategy Behind the Shake-Up

These updates are part of a cohesive strategy from Delta to streamline its operations and deepen digital engagement.

  • The Hawaiian Split Was Inevitable: With Alaska Airlines acquiring Hawaiian, dissolving partnerships with competitors like Delta was a predictable business move. For travelers, it reduces choice and highlights the need to diversify your points across different airline alliances and bank programs.
  • The App-Only Push is Strategic: By forcing its best customers to use the app for high-value interactions, Delta increases app adoption and gathers more data, creating a direct channel for marketing and future offers [Source: Forbes].
  • The Value of Co-Branded Credit Cards: These changes emphasize the stability of co-branded credit cards. Cards like the Delta SkyMiles® Reserve American Express Card are crucial tools for earning status and accessing benefits that are becoming more tightly controlled. The perks from these cards are now more valuable than ever [Source: The Points Guy].

Your Immediate To-Do List

  • Review Hawaiian Travel Plans: If you plan to use SkyMiles on Hawaiian Airlines, you must book your ticket by June 30, 2025. Be certain about your dates.
  • Download the Fly Delta App: If you are a Platinum or Diamond member (or expect to be), download the app now and familiarize yourself with the interface for selecting your Choice Benefits.
  • Diversify Your Points Strategy: This is a clear reminder not to keep all your points in one airline's basket. Flexible points from Chase, Amex, or Capital One provide crucial insulation from these loyalty program shifts.

The window to use SkyMiles on Hawaiian Airlines is closing, and the gateway to Delta's best perks is now in your pocket. By acting on this information, you can navigate these changes without missing a beat.

title: Citi Reimagines Its No-Fee Lineup with the New Strata Card, Targeting Everyday Spenders and Travelers Alike
imageAlt: The new Citi Strata Card representing a strategic shift in rewards for consumers.
author: Financial Advisor, Travelcardinsider
snippet: Citi is retiring the Rewards+® Card and launching the no-annual-fee Citi Strata Card, featuring up to 5X points on travel and robust 3X categories for everyday spending, with a clear transition plan for existing cardholders and new applicants.
content:
Citi Reimagines Its No-Fee Lineup with the New Strata Card, Targeting Everyday Spenders and Travelers Alike

NEW YORK, NY – In a strategic move set to ripple through the wallets of savvy American consumers, Citi has officially pulled back the curtain on a significant evolution in its credit card portfolio. The bank is retiring its long-standing Citi Rewards+® Card and channelling its features into a brand-new, no-annual-fee product: the Citi Strata Card.

This isn't a mere name change. It’s a fundamental overhaul designed to create a rewards powerhouse that aggressively competes for top-of-wallet status. With a potent combination of up to 5X points on travel and broad 3X categories covering daily essentials like groceries and gas, the Citi Strata Card is making a bold statement in the crowded no-fee card market. For more details, you can refer to Citi's Official Announcement.

For years, consumers have sought a single, no-fee card that generously rewards both their travel ambitions and their routine spending. With this launch, Citi is signaling its intent to deliver just that.

The Transition Roadmap: What to Expect

Following the closure of the Citi Rewards+® Card to new applicants this past April, Citi has established a clear and transparent timeline for the transition.

  • For Existing Citi Rewards+® Cardholders: Your account will automatically be converted to the new Citi Strata Card on July 20, 2025. No action is needed on your part; the change will be seamless.
  • For New Applicants: The wait won't be long. Direct applications for the Citi Strata Card are scheduled to open in late 2025.

It's vital for consumers to distinguish this new no-fee card from its sibling, the Citi Strata Premier℠ Card. The Premier version carries a $95 annual fee and, in return, offers a different rewards structure and, crucially, access to a wider array of high-value travel transfer partners. You can review the details on the Citi Strata Premier℠ Card Official Product Page.

Under the Hood: A Breakdown of the New Rewards Engine

The earning structure of the Citi Strata Card represents a monumental leap forward from its predecessor. Citi has clearly listened to consumer demand for rewards on a wider array of spending. The new earning rates are as follows:

  • 5X ThankYou® Points on hotels, car rentals, and attractions when booked through the Citi Travel portal.
  • 3X ThankYou® Points at supermarkets.
  • 3X ThankYou® Points on select transit, which includes subways, ride-sharing services, ferries, and more.
  • 3X ThankYou® Points at both traditional gas stations and Electric Vehicle (EV) charging stations.
  • 3X ThankYou® Points on one eligible self-selected category from the following choices:
    • Fitness clubs and gym memberships
    • Select streaming services
    • Live entertainment (concerts, sporting events, theater)
    • Cosmetic stores, barbershops, and hair salons
    • Pet supply stores
  • 2X ThankYou® Points at restaurants.
  • 1X ThankYou® Points on all other purchases.

This multi-tiered system transforms the card from a niche product into a versatile tool for nearly every type of consumer, from the daily commuter to the frequent traveler.

Putting It to the Test: A Weekend Trip Reimagined

Let's illustrate the card's power with a practical example. Imagine a family planning a weekend escape:

  • Hotel: They book a two-night stay for $400 via the Citi Travel portal.
    Points Earned: $400 x 5 = 2,000 ThankYou® Points
  • Fuel: They spend $60 to fill up their car for the road trip.
    Points Earned: $60 x 3 = 180 ThankYou® Points
  • Groceries: A quick $50 stop at a supermarket for road trip snacks and drinks.
    Points Earned: $50 x 3 = 150 ThankYou® Points
  • Dining Out: They enjoy several meals over the weekend, totaling $150.
    Points Earned: $150 x 2 = 300 ThankYou® Points
  • Future Plans: Having previously selected 'Live Entertainment' as their 3X choice category, they purchase $100 in concert tickets for an upcoming show.
    Points Earned: $100 x 3 = 300 ThankYou® Points

On total spending of $760, this family would earn a remarkable 2,930 ThankYou® Points. This scenario highlights how effectively the card accumulates rewards across a spectrum of common spending categories.

A Calculated Farewell: The Features Left Behind

From a financial advisor's perspective, this transition is a classic case of simplification over specialization. To achieve this broad appeal, Citi is jettisoning two unique—and for some, beloved—perks of the old Rewards+ Card. For the vast majority of users, these features will be discontinued:

  • The 10% Points Rebate: The signature benefit that returned 10% of your points on the first 100,000 points redeemed annually is being retired.
  • The 'Round Up' Feature: The perk that rounded up rewards on every purchase to the nearest 10 points is also going away.

These features, while clever, added a layer of complexity. By removing them, Citi is betting that a straightforward, high-earning structure is more valuable to a wider audience. It’s a trade-off that pits quirky, niche benefits against raw, easy-to-understand earning power. There is, however, a small exception: Cardholders who opened a Citi Rewards+® Card between July 20, 2024, and July 19, 2025, will be granted a one-year grace period, retaining these two legacy features until July 19, 2026. This has been confirmed through Citi's official communication to Rewards+ Cardholders.

Unlocking True Value: The Redemption Playbook

ThankYou® Points earned with the Citi Strata Card are flexible. They can be redeemed for cash back, statement credits, or gift cards at a standard value of 1 cent per point, as detailed on the Citi ThankYou Rewards Program Official Site.

However, for travel enthusiasts, the ultimate goal is often transferring points to airline and hotel loyalty programs. This is where a strategic approach is essential. Points from the no-fee Citi Strata Card can be transferred to a select group of partners, including Choice Privileges, JetBlue TrueBlue, and Wyndham Rewards. To unlock Citi's full and more lucrative suite of airline partners—such as Virgin Atlantic Flying Club, Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer, and Air France/KLM Flying Blue—you must pair the Strata Card with a premium ThankYou® card, namely the Citi Strata Premier℠ Card. This 'card pairing' strategy allows you to earn points rapidly with the no-fee card's powerful multipliers and then transfer them out at maximum value through the premium card.

The Financial Advisor's Verdict & What's Next

The upcoming Citi Strata Card is poised to be a dominant force in the no-annual-fee credit card arena. By delivering robust rewards on travel, transit, and everyday spending, Citi has crafted a product that will appeal to a massive segment of U.S. consumers.

While the loss of the old Rewards+ perks is a noteworthy trade-off, the new high-earning, simplified structure is a significant net positive. This card is ideal for:

  • Individuals seeking their first serious rewards credit card.
  • Families looking to maximize rewards on essential spending like groceries and gas.
  • Travelers who can leverage the Citi Travel portal for 5X earnings.
  • Existing Citi customers looking to build a powerful card combination.

New applicants can look forward to an attractive launch offer in late 2025:

  • Welcome Offer: Earn 30,000 ThankYou® Points after spending $1,000 in the first 3 months. This is a simple, direct value of $300 in cash back.
  • Introductory APR: A 0% intro APR on purchases and balance transfers for 15 months, after which a variable APR of 19.24%-29.24% will apply, as per the Official Citi Strata Card Terms and Conditions.

The Citi Strata Card is not just a rebranded product; it's a strategic realignment. It signals that Citi is ready to compete fiercely for the everyday spending of the American consumer, and for those who play their cards right, the rewards are waiting.

Disclaimer: Information is current as of the article's publication date. Card benefits, terms, and offers are subject to change. Please refer to the official Citi website for the latest details.

title: Hilton's "Points Plus" Promo: A Goldmine for Frequent Travelers or a Dud for Vacationers?
imageAlt: Hilton hotel exterior with Points Plus promotion branding
author: Travelcardinsider Staff
snippet: Our financial analysis breaks down Hilton's summer offer to reveal who really benefits—and how to maximize your earnings before the August 15 deadline.
content:
As the summer travel season kicks into high gear, Hilton Honors has launched its new global promotion, "Points Plus." On the surface, it’s a simple offer: earn 1,000 bonus points for every stay. But as savvy travelers know, the value of any promotion is in the details. Unlike the flashy "double points" offers of the past, this flat-bonus structure creates a clear divide. For some, it's a fantastic way to rack up extra points. For others, it’s a barely-there blip on the radar. As your trusted advisors at Travelcardinsider, we’re here to dissect this promotion, show you the math, and provide a clear strategy to help you decide if "Points Plus" is right for you.

The Nuts and Bolts: How "Points Plus" Works

Hilton has kept this promotion refreshingly simple. Here are the essential details:

  • The Bonus: Earn a flat 1,000 Bonus Points per eligible stay.
  • Promotion Period: Valid for all stays completed between June 1, 2025, and August 15, 2025.
  • Registration is Mandatory: This is the most crucial step. You must register for the promotion at the official Hilton Honors website before your stay. It’s a quick, one-time action.
  • No Earning Cap: There is no limit to the total bonus points you can accumulate.
  • Reward Stays Qualify: In a generous move, stays booked with points (or Points & Money) are still eligible to earn the 1,000-point bonus.
  • What Defines a "Stay"? A "stay" is one or more consecutive nights at the same hotel. Checking out and back in doesn't create a new stay.

This represents a clear strategic shift from Hilton. Instead of rewarding high spenders, the focus this summer is squarely on rewarding frequency.

Financial Advisor's Breakdown: Who Wins?

From a financial perspective, the "Points Plus" promotion is not one-size-fits-all. The flat 1,000-point bonus heavily favors travelers with multiple, short, and often inexpensive stays.

The Clear Winner: The "Road Warrior" and Weekend Explorer

Anyone whose travel involves frequent one or two-night stops will find this promotion to be a lucrative boost.

  • Real-World Example: A consultant has three separate one-night stays in a week.
  • Stay 1 (Mon): Hampton Inn, $140. Earns 1,400 base points + 1,000 bonus points.
  • Stay 2 (Wed): Hilton Garden Inn, $165. Earns 1,650 base points + 1,000 bonus points.
  • Stay 3 (Fri): Homewood Suites, $180. Earns 1,800 base points + 1,000 bonus points.
  • Total Promo Bonus: 3,000 points on a total spend of $485.

Here, the bonus provides a significant return relative to the amount spent.

The Loser: The Long-Stay Vacationer

Conversely, travelers planning a single, extended vacation will see minimal benefit.

  • Real-World Example: A family books a seven-night stay at a resort for $3,500.
  • They will earn an impressive 35,000 base points.
  • Total Promo Bonus: A mere 1,000 points.

While 1,000 points is better than nothing, it's a drop in the bucket. To understand the real-world value, it's helpful to know what your points are worth. You can do this with the Official Hilton Honors Points Explorer Tool.

Pro-Tips: A 4-Step Strategy to Maximize Earnings

If your travel style fits the bill, a little strategy can help you squeeze every last point out of this promotion.

  1. Register Immediately: Head to the Hilton Honors website now and register. There is no downside, and it ensures you won't miss out on points for a last-minute trip.
  2. Always Book Direct: To be eligible, you must book your stay through official Hilton channels (Hilton.com, the Honors app, or by phone). Bookings via third-party sites like Expedia are not eligible. Booking direct also ensures you receive other benefits like the Price Match Guarantee.
  3. Consider the "Hotel Hop": For dedicated points maximizers, this strategy can pay off. If you're in a city with multiple Hilton properties for several nights, booking each night at a different hotel will trigger the 1,000-point bonus each time. It’s an extra effort, but it turns a single bonus into multiple bonuses.
  4. The Ultimate Strategy: Stacking Your Earnings

    This is where a modest bonus becomes a massive points haul. The "Points Plus" bonus can be stacked with elite status bonuses and co-branded credit card earnings.

    • The Stack Explained: Base Points + Promo Bonus + Elite Status Bonus + Credit Card Bonus.

    Let's revisit that one-night, $165 stay for a Diamond member with the Hilton Honors Aspire Card:

    • Base Points: 1,650
    • Diamond Bonus (100%): +1,650 points
    • "Points Plus" Promo: +1,000 points
    • Aspire Card Earnings (14x): +2,310 points (as per the Official American Express Hilton Card Benefits Page)
    • Total for one night: 6,610 Hilton Honors points.

    This is how a simple bonus becomes part of a powerful points-earning machine.

Our Verdict: A Strategic Play for the Right Traveler

Hilton's "Points Plus" promotion isn't the most exciting offer ever, but it's a solid and predictable incentive. It clearly rewards frequency, making it a valuable tool for business travelers and weekend adventurers. For those planning one long vacation, this promo is a minor perk, not a decision-maker. The key for everyone is to understand its structure, register before staying, and align it with your travel plans. Every point counts, and Hilton is offering an easy way to grab an extra thousand with every check-in this summer.

Disclaimer: Always review the full terms and conditions for any loyalty promotion on the official Hilton Honors website. Bonus points earned do not count toward elite tier qualification. For more on how regulations can affect these programs, see our report on the future of credit card rewards.

title: The End of an Era: Southwest Airlines Introduces Bag Fees, But a New Points Promotion Offers a Silver Lining
imageAlt: Southwest Airlines aircraft symbolizing a new era of travel
author: Travelcardinsider Staff
snippet: Southwest Airlines ends its iconic 'Bags Fly Free' policy for some fares, introducing new fees. To soften the blow, a new promotion offers up to 20,000 bonus Rapid Rewards points, fundamentally changing the value equation for travelers.
content:
For Immediate Release

DALLAS, TX – June 22, 2025 – For decades, it was the marketing mantra that defined a beloved American airline: "Bags Fly Free." That simple promise from Southwest Airlines has officially been grounded. In a landmark shift, Southwest has implemented fees for checked baggage on its lowest fares, a strategic pivot that fundamentally reshapes its value proposition. The new policy, affecting all reservations from May 28, 2025, signals a new, more intricate chapter for the carrier.

However, the airline is also extending a potentially lucrative olive branch. To temper the news, Southwest has unveiled a targeted promotion offering up to 20,000 bonus Rapid Rewards points for summer travel. This creates a new calculus for American travelers: the all-inclusive Southwest of yesterday is gone, replaced by a landscape where strategic planning, elite status, and co-branded credit cards are more crucial than ever.

Deconstructing the New Baggage Policy

The once-unconditional "Bags Fly Free" slogan now carries a significant asterisk. For travelers booking "Basic" and "Wanna Get Away" fares, the following fees now apply for checked luggage:

  • First Checked Bag: $35
  • Second Checked Bag: $45

This change most acutely impacts budget-conscious travelers and families. However, not all customers will pay. Southwest has maintained its free baggage allowance for its most loyal customers and premium fare buyers. According to Southwest Airlines, the following passengers will continue to enjoy complimentary checked bags [Southwest Airlines' official baggage policy page]:

  • Two Free Checked Bags: Business Select customers and A-List Preferred Members.
  • One Free Checked Bag: A-List Members and primary holders of Southwest Rapid Rewards® Credit Cards from Chase.

To illustrate, a family of four with one checked bag each would previously have paid $0. Under the new system, without status or a qualifying credit card, that same family faces a hefty $280 in baggage fees for a round-trip journey. This kind of change underscores the importance of understanding how loyalty programs are evolving across the industry.

A Summer of Opportunity: The 20,000 Bonus Points Promotion

To soften the blow, Southwest has launched a targeted promotion for Rapid Rewards members. Eligible travelers who register can earn substantial bonus points for flights between June 11 and August 31, 2025. The promotion is tiered, as detailed on the airline's promotional page [official promotion registration page]:

  • Fly 1 round trip (or 2 one-ways): Earn 5,000 bonus points.
  • Fly 2 round trips (or 4 one-ways): Earn an additional 5,000 bonus points (10,000 total).
  • Fly 3 round trips (or 6 one-ways): Earn another 10,000 bonus points (20,000 total).

Significantly, these bonus points count toward qualifying for the coveted Southwest Companion Pass®, though they do not contribute to A-List or A-List Preferred status.

A Financial Advisor's Perspective: The New Value Equation

This is a calculated trade-off. Southwest is betting the revenue from bag fees will outweigh any customer attrition. For travelers, the equation for value has changed, similar to shifts seen in the broader credit card rewards landscape.

Revisiting the family of four, the new $280 fee is a substantial cost. However, if one parent holds a Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card, the first checked bag for them and up to eight companions on the same booking is free. This single benefit negates the fee, making the card's $149 annual fee an immediate money-saver. When combined with the summer promotion, that family earns 5,000 bonus points (worth ~$65-$75), turning a new cost into a net gain.

For a solo traveler, the math is even more direct. A single round trip would incur $70 in bag fees. The 5,000-point bonus, worth roughly the same, effectively cancels out this new cost. For those who already get free bags via status or a credit card, this promotion is pure upside, much like the simple bonuses in other programs like the Hilton "Points Plus" promo.

Navigating Other Key Updates

The introduction of baggage fees is part of a broader evolution. Travelers should note these other changes:

  • New Fare Structure: A restrictive "Basic" fare debuted on May 28. Other fares will be rebranded later this year. More details can be found on Southwest's website.
  • The End of Non-Expiring Flight Credits: For tickets booked on or after May 28, 2025, resulting flight credits will expire in one year or less. The era of indefinite credits is over for new bookings. You can find more information about this on the page for the new flight credit policy.
  • Dynamic Award Pricing: Since March 2025, the points required for an award flight vary more significantly based on demand, mirroring other airlines' pricing models.

Actionable Advice for the Modern Southwest Traveler

  • Check Your Eligibility: The 20,000-point promotion is targeted. Log in to your Rapid Rewards account and visit the promotions page to register before booking.
  • A Co-Branded Credit Card is Now Essential: For anyone flying Southwest annually with a checked bag, a co-branded credit card has become a near necessity. The first-bag-free benefit is the most effective way to circumvent these new fees. Explore options on the Chase website. It is a reminder of how crucial it is to find the smartest cards for booking your travel.
  • Chase the Companion Pass: With the bonus points counting towards the Companion Pass, this summer is a prime opportunity to earn this valuable perk, which allows a companion to fly for just taxes and fees. Review the requirements on Southwest's site. The issuer, Chase, has other valuable cards to consider; see how to maximize Chase Freedom bonuses for your travel fund.
  • Be Mindful of Expiration Dates: Pay close attention to the new flight credit policy to avoid losing value on canceled flights.

Conclusion: A More Complex, Yet Rewarding, Journey

The Southwest Airlines known for its simplicity is transforming. The introduction of bag fees ends a defining era. However, the airline is not abandoning loyalty. New promotions and the powerful, fee-negating benefits of its credit cards create a new playbook for the astute traveler. The journey with Southwest is no longer as simple, but for those who understand the new rules and leverage the tools available, there is still immense value to be discovered.

Your guide to leveraging Amex Offers for significant savings on flights, hotels, and more this travel season.

What Are Amex Offers and Why Should You Care?

Amex Offers are targeted discounts providing statement credits or bonus Membership Rewards points for purchases at specific merchants. The process is seamless: add the offer to your eligible American Express card, make a qualifying purchase, and the savings automatically appear on your account. It's a frictionless method for saving money on expenses you were likely to incur anyway.

From a financial planning perspective, consistently utilizing Amex Offers is a cornerstone of maximizing your American Express card's value. The current lineup for summer 2025 is particularly robust for travelers, making it an opportune time to pay close attention to this benefit.

Sizzling Summer Stays: Hot Hotel & Resort Offers

Escape to Paradise with Hilton Savings

Financial Advisor's Corner: The Art of Stacking Your Savings

    • You earn 3,600 Membership Rewards points (at 3x on travel).

By layering these strategies, you've combined a cash discount, a statement credit, and bonus points on a single transaction. This is how savvy travelers turn a good deal into a great one.
